declared_in: reports/decision.md, section "Evaluation round 3 (written Nov 15, 2026, before any item below was scored)"
git_dirty_source_means: a file under src/ or a Python file in app/ differed from git_commit
what: The pre-season trigger with one decision per county per year. The value of a rule is (drought seasons caught - cost ratio x firings) / decisions; higher is better, so a difference above zero favours the forecast.
history: the full table of monthly issue rows (Rio Grande rows of it), so the class-frequency rule has the years before the first test year

value_differences.name: forecast value minus 'D1 or worse now' value at cost ratio 0.02
value_differences.rows_used: Rio Grande outlooks issued in March, one per county per year (scored rows)
value_differences.year_unit: the calendar year of the issue date (the date the forecast was made), all counties together
value_differences.statistic: mean over rows (yearly means weighted by rows)

block1.caveat: Percentile interval from 18 resampled years (block 1). With this few years it is too narrow: in simulation a nominal 95% interval covered the truth about 88% of the time with 8 years and 92% with 18 (80% and 90% with two-year blocks), and is expected to be less if years are dependent. These coverage figures come from a simulation with independent years and a true difference of zero, not from this project's data.
